project_name: NextEra’s Mason County Wind Energy Project
evidence_note: Opened 2026-10-08: Ledger Independent (Maysville Online), 'NextEra cancels plans for wind farm in Mason County', published 2014-05-23, reproducing in full the letter from Mark David Goss, counsel for NextEra Energy Resources, to Mason County Attorney John F. Estill (the letter itself bears no date in the reproduction). It states: 'As a result of the enactment of House Bill 291 and the activities of the Mason County Planning and Zoning Commission, NextEra has no choice but to discontinue the Mason County project effective immediately', and 'please accept this letter as formal notification of such discontinuance.' The letter itself gives its reasons: House Bill 291 and the 'very restrictive setback provisions' the Mason County Planning and Zoning Commission was likely to enact. It replies to the county's April 25, 2014 request for a public meeting under HB 291. Matches the record (NextEra, Mason County, May 2014, state and anticipated local restrictions). This is the developer's letter as printed in the local paper; the county's copy was not located.

Opened 2026-10-08: Town of Woodland, NC official page 'Solar Farm Projects Located Near Woodland, Update December 14, 2015'. It states the town board had approved rezoning from RA to M2 for three solar sites (White Farm, Burgwyn Farm, Outland Farm) and that 'At the December 3, 2015, Town Board Meeting ... the town board voted to maintain the RA zone for the fourth proposed solar farm site', 42 acres at the east entrance off State Highway 258, a denial 'due, in part, to a circulated petition', because approval 'would create a situation in which the town would be completely surrounded by solar farms.' The page does not name the developer (the record says Strata Solar; search snippets from Governing and the Roanoke-Chowan News-Herald, not read, name Strata and say a moratorium was also voted). The page does not mention the moratorium itself, so the moratorium is not confirmed by a document read; the denial of the fourth project is. EIA-860M lists plant 59175 'Woodland Solar', 5 MW, Northampton County, operating 4/2016, which is probably one of the three approved sites, not the denied one; no document links it to the denied site.

project_name: Skipjack Wind Farm Interconnection Facility in Fenwick State Park
evidence_note: Opened 2026-10-08: Orsted (developer) press release on the Skipjack Wind site, 'Orsted Announces Pivot Away from Fenwick Island State Park', dated 10.07.2020 (10 July 2020, European date format). Text: 'Orsted has notified DNREC that it will no longer pursue plans to build the interconnection facility at Fenwick Island State Park as initially proposed.' Reason stated by the developer: 'a large portion of the site is comprised of undisturbed wetlands.' It refers to the July 2019 non-binding MOU with Delaware DNREC and describes Skipjack as a 120 MW offshore wind farm 19 miles off the Maryland-Delaware coast. Matches the record (interconnection facility at Fenwick Island State Park abandoned in 2020). This is the developer's own announcement, not an agency decision; no federal decision document addresses the Fenwick site (the BOEM Maryland Offshore Wind page I read concerns US Wind's separate lease OCS-A 0490 and is not this project). The release attributes the change to wetlands, not to Surfrider or other opposition. The outcome applies to the Fenwick Island interconnection site only; the release says Orsted would pursue an alternative site.

'The Selected Alternative consists of the proposed 485 MW PV solar plant on 4,138 acres of BLM-administered public land', converted from the 1,000 MW solar thermal project approved in 2010 on 6,831 acres, 8 miles west of Blythe. NAME CHECK as requested: neither the BLM ROD notice, the DOI release, nor EIA uses 'Blythe Mesa' for this NextEra project; they all call it the 'Blythe Solar Power Project' / Blythe Solar 110, II, III, IV, and the BLM ROD names the grant holder 'NextEra Blythe Solar Energy Center, LLC'. The record's details (NextEra, 465 to 485 MW, about 4,070 acres of BLM land, built 2015 to 2020, CRIT 2014 suit) describe the NextEra Blythe Solar Power Project, so the record's name 'Blythe Mesa' appears to be wrong.

project_name: New York Bight Offshore Wind Area
evidence_note: Opened 2026-10-08: BOEM 'New York Bight' page (updated 2026-01-08). 'In March 2021, BOEM identified nearly 800,000 acres as Wind Energy Areas (WEAs) in the New York Bight'. 'On Feb. 23, 2022, BOEM held an offshore wind auction for six lease areas in the New York Bight. The lease sale drew competitive winning bids from six companies totaling approximately $4.37 billion', with six executed leases (OCS-A 0537 Bluepoint Wind, 0538 Attentive Energy, 0539 Community Offshore Wind, 0541 Atlantic Shores Bight, 0542 Invenergy, 0544 Vineyard Mid-Atlantic; executed May 2022). Final Programmatic EIS October 2024; Programmatic ROD December 2, 2024, which 'does not approve any activities'. Latest item: a January 15, 2025 NOI for the Vineyard Mid-Atlantic COP EIS, whose public meetings were cancelled under the January 2025 presidential memorandum that temporarily halted offshore wind leasing and paused new approvals. So the designation the plaintiffs challenged stands, and leases were issued: the WEA designation and leasing went forward. Matches the record (BOEM New York Bight WEAs off New Jersey). Caveat: no individual project in these leases has a COP approval, and new approvals are paused; this outcome describes the area designation and leasing only. The 2023 lawsuit's later course was not checked.
